 11/14 Preview – Panarin out for “family reasons”, Turcotte checks in + 12/56/40 Line, Latest on Gustafsson, Kuemper 500 Ceremony
 By Zach Dooley 
 7 hours ago 
 326 Comments 
 Share This Article 
 Share This Article 
 WHO: Los Angeles Kings (5-10-2) vs. Calgary Flames (8-10-1)
 WHAT: 2026-27 NHL Regular Season, Game 18/84
 WHEN: Saturday, November 14 @ 7:00 PM Pacific
 WHERE: Crypto.com Arena – Los Angeles, CA
HOW TO FOLLOW: VIDEO: ABTV, DAZN – VIDEO: 830 AM KLAA, ESPN LA App, LA Kings App – TWITTER: @dooleylak & @lakings 
 TODAY’S MATCHUP: The Kings conclude what has been a disappointing, seven-game homestand to date, as they host the Calgary Flames in Pacific Division showdown. 
 HEAD-TO-HEAD: Forward Quinton Byfield led the Kings last season with three goals against the Flames, while Byfield (3-1-4) and forward Alex Laferriere (1-3-4) tied for the team lead with four points apiece. Additionally, forward Trevor Moore collected three assists in the four games played, while forward Adrian Kempe scored two goals. 
 KINGS VITALS: As per Peter Laviolette yesterday, the Kings held an optional practice on Friday, followed by a mandatory morning skate earlier today at Toyota Sports Performance Center. 
 The Kings will turn back to goaltender Anton Forsberg for the homestand finale this evening against Calgary. Forsberg has made five career appearances against the Flames, bringing with him a record of 2-3-0, with a .901 save percentage and a 2.91 goals-against average. 
 Here is a projected lineup for tonight’s game, based on today’s morning skate –
 Turcotte – Laferriere – Kempe
Fiala – Byfield – Zuccarello
Moore – Haula – Armia
Lee – Laughton – Perry
 Anderson – Doughty
Dumoulin – Clarke
Edmundson – Ceci
 Forsberg
Kuemper
 Forward Artemi Panarin will not play today due to family reasons. Look for forward Alex Turcotte to check into the lineup, skating in Panarin’s spot,. Defenseman Erik Gustafsson does not appear like he will play tonight, his third game missed due to a day-to-day injury. 
 FLAMES VITALS: After a 1-2-0 record on a recent three-game homestand, Calgary begins a three-game roadtrip tonight in Los Angeles, before visits to Anaheim and San Jose in the coming days. 
 Per Derek Wills of the Calgary radio broadcast, here’s how the Flames lined up last time out versus the Rangers – 
 #Flames vs. #NYR Farabee-Backlund-Coronato Sharangovich-Frost-Suniev Gridin-Pospisil-Strome Othmann-Castagna-Klapka Hanley-Nemec Middleton-Whitecloud Kuznetsov-Parekh Cooley (Starter) Wolf https://t.co/EsyvEggxNF
 — Derek Wills (@dwillsnhl) November 12, 2026 
 Calgary won three of the four meetings against Los Angeles last season, though the lone Kings victory came here at Crypto.com Arena. Forward Joel Farabee is Calgary’s early-season leader in goals (7), points (17) and power-play points (9), coming in his second full season with the Flames. Farabee scored the last time these teams met – a 3-1 Calgary win in April – and has four career goals versus Los Angeles. 
 Storyline Of The Day – Panarin Update + Adjustments 
Had a storyline here about how the Kings finally got a look at what having Artemi Panarin and Kevin Fiala in the same lineup looked like. Had some things written about how the power play specifically looked, with Panarin on the left flank and Fiala on the right flank. The results were pretty exciting, especially on the 5-on-3 goal the Kings scored last game, with quick decision making from both Fiala and Panarin resulting in a slam-dunk rebound goal for Quinton Byfield in front of the net. 
 Quinton Byfield pulls the Kings within one goal 👑 Catch all the action on Sportsnet 📺 https://t.co/K106sqOXws
 — Sportsnet (@Sportsnet) November 13, 2026 
 Then came today’s morning skate, when Peter Laviolette noted that Panarin will be away from the team tonight due to family reasons. Naturally, first thoughts when you hear something like that are with Panarin and his family. Not sure the situation beyond Laviolette’s update today, nor is it any of our business what the situation is. Just hoping all is as good as it can be for him and his family, which is always the number-one priority, so sending well wishes his way. 
 In terms of how that impacts tonight’s lineup for the Kings, well, there will naturally need to be some changes. 
 Panarin has the ability to play on instincts and he creates off of those instincts in ways most cannot. To write it how I’d usually say it, if the Kings had another Panarin-type of player available, he would already be in the lineup. So, you can’t just find a 1-for-1 replacement for a player of his ability. You have to shuffle do something differently. 
 At 5-on-5, it was Alex Turcotte skating in that spot. Turcotte’s best stretch in the NHL came when playing with Adrian Kempe during the 2024-25 season. The options when you lose a player of Panarin are limited, but Turcotte is a player who was out of the lineup who has shown an ability to connect with higher-end players. I actually think he’s clicked with Laferriere in short stretches also. Part of what you’re looking for is a player who has shown an ability to compliment high-end players, especially if you can get that player without disrupting other lines that worked. That is what Turcotte has done in the past and that’s the hope with Turcotte tonight. 
 “I think that’s been his MO his whole life, is a guy that can come out and create some offense,” Laviolette said of Turcotte. “Coming off an injury that was lengthy, he came back in the lineup, came out of the lineup, got a few more days of being on the ice in practice, got some conditioning and I think this is a great spot for him to come in and do his best to have an impact on the game. Playing with a couple of our high-end players, I think it’s a good spot for him and a great opportunity for him.”
 With the power play, again, you can’t just replace Panarin. He is a unique, 1-of-1 player, who creates a system more than he just plays within one. During today’s morning skate, defenseman Brandt Clarke jumped up onto that unit, operating at the top. He joined Fiala, Byfield, Adrian Kempe and Alex Laferriere on that unit. On the second unit, the Kings practiced today with Drew Doughty, Mats Zuccarello, Corey Perry, Erik Haula and one of Turcotte or forward Trevor Moore. 
 I think Turcotte has the biggest opportunity in this equation.
 Obviously when Panarin comes back, he will play 20 minutes a night, as Laviolette said today. But before his injury, it was Turcotte who won the second-line center job out of training camp. The Kings have decisions to make up front, players who could find themselves out of the lineup or even potentially on waivers when everyone is back. For Turcotte, it’s an opportunity to show he should be among the players forcing the decision to come on other players.
 “There’s no question when Panarin comes back, he’ll be inserted into 20 minutes again, but he’s not here, so it’s a chance for [Turcotte],” Laviolette added. “He was given those looks, given those opportunities before his injury. For him to come back and get that look again, I think it can give confidence to him as a player. It can help our team be successful. If he does have that impact in a game that we’re looking for, those are things that help you stay in the lineup and take on more minutes, more responsibility and be a contributor.” 
 3 To Watch For – 
– I thought the best Kings line at even strength on Thursday was the Moore/Haula/Armia line. Think that is supported both by the eye test and the numbers. 
 “I thought that the Haula line was pretty good [against New York], I thought they were very noticeable,” Peter Laviolette said. “With a little bit of health coming back, that was the first opportunity and chance they had to really take on that role. I thought all three of them were good. I thought the whole line was good for what I asked them to do. I thought they accomplished that. I thought that they were the most noticeable line that night.”
 In terms of the metrics, that line was on the ice for 12 shot attempts for and three against at 5-on-5, with a 3-0 Kings advantage in high-danger chances and one goal for, compared to none against. It was the only 5-on-5 goal the Kings scored, on top of the power-play goal mentioned above. 
 On paper, this is what having Fiala back should do for the team’s alignment up front. It puts a player like Moore – who I felt was the best Kings forward on Thursday – on a matchup-capable third line. A line Laviolette said he wants to be an identity line for the team. Moore has been in that role a ton in his time with the Kings, while Haula and Armia have played that role often in their careers. The Kings have their two scoring lines and if this line can pull their weight, it’s a matchup line to compliment those two units, while chipping in with some offense of their own, as Moore did with his goal versus the Islanders. 
 “I feel like last game was something we can really build off off, I think we set the standard for our line last game,” Haula added. “As a whole, for us individually, it’s something to go back on. That’s the goal for tonight too, is to keep that up……we want to be a consistent line for the team.”
 I’m glad the Kings didn’t break that line up with Panarin out. They were really good. Keep them together and see what Turcotte can do on the top line, adjusting as needed. But to start, let’s see if Moore, Haula and Armia can get something going again tonight. 
 – Regarding defenseman Erik Gustafsson, he practiced yesterday during an optional day for the team on the ice and was with the group this morning as well.
 We don’t have a ton of information on what has kept Gustafsson out of action, minus the “day-to-day” designation he’s been given by Laviolette. Gustafsson has been a nice addition for the Kings this season, offering puck movement on the blueline that the team certainly has missed in the two games he’s been out. 
 Where I believe Gustafsson has most been missed is on the breakout. Per SportLOGIQ, Gustafsson ranks second among Kings defensemen in zone controlled zone exits, both via carryouts and via the pass, on a per-game basis. Similarly related, Gustafsson ranks second on the team in offensive-zone entries with possession as well. 
 That’s his game. He transports pucks well and moves pucks efficiently. Strengths that were weaknesses for the group last season. While it does not appear as if he’ll be ready for tonight, seems like at the very least he should be in a position to travel with the team on their upcoming roadtrip, which is a good sign he should feature on the East Coast. 
 – Lastly, tonight’s puck drop will be slightly delayed for a pre-game ceremony in recognition of goaltender Darcy Kuemper reaching 500 career regular-season games played. 
 “I feel honored to have played that many games in this league,” Kuemper said. “It’s pretty special and I’m grateful for every game I’ve gotten to play.”
 Kuemper became the 87th goaltender in NHL history to reach the milestone. I didn’t realize how rare 500 games was for a goaltender, compared to 1,000 games for a skater, but for reference, 423 players have reached 1,000 games played as a forward or a defenseman. So, for Kuemper to reach that number shows longevity and enough caliber in his play to remain in the league for as long as he has. 
 The pre-game ceremony will include members of his family as well as a few additional guests and will occur before puck drop on the ice. The opportunity to celebrate with those closest to him is something Kuemper is very much looking forward to. 
 “Without them, I don’t think I would have been able to do it,” he added. “Your family is your rock and they’re with you the whole way. It’s going to be very, very special to be able to share it with them.”
 One last game here at home before the team hits the road for a four-game trip, beginning on Tuesday in Boston. The Kings have already wasted an opportunity here at home to turn their record around with a strong homestand, with a below .500 record already guaranteed, with tonight the final game before heading East. 7 PM puck drop, before the Sunday morning plane ride.
